Article.ArticleTitle: Pharmaceutical Product Lead Optimization for Better In Vivo Bioequivalence Performance: A case study of Diclofenac Sodium Extended Release Matrix Tablets.

Abstract.AbstractText: In order to prove the validity of a new formulation, a considerable amount of efforts is required to study bioequivalence, not only increases the burden of carrying out a number of bioequivalence studies but eventually increase the cost of the optimization process.

The aim of the present study was to develop sustained release matrix tablets containing diclofenac sodium using natural polymers and to demonstrate step by step process of product development till the prediction of in vivo marketed product equivalence of the developed product.

Different batches of tablets were prepared by direct compression. In vitro drug release studies were performed as per USP. The drug release data were assessed using model-dependent, model-independent and convolution approaches.

Drug release profiles showed that SR action were in the following order: Gum Tragacanth > Sodium Alginate > Gum Acacia. Amongst different batches prepared, only F1 and F8 were passed the USP criteria of the drug release. Developed formulas were found to fit Higuchi kinetics model with Fickian (case I) diffusion-mediated release mechanism. Model- independent kinetics model confirmed that total of four batched were passed depending on the similarity factors based on the comparison with the marketed Diclofenac. The results of in vivo predictive convolution model indicated that predicted AUC, Cmax and Tmax values for batch F8 were similar to that of marketed product.

This study provides simple yet effective outline of pharmaceutical product development process that will minimize the formulation development trials and maximize the product success in bioequivalence studies.
